summary.headline: Bhagyanagar India Q1 FY27: revenue above ₹700 crore and EBITDA margin a record 5.43%, but volume fell to 5,200-5,278 tons on April-May supply disruption.
summary.overview: Management reported revenue of over ₹700 crore, PAT of ₹20 crore (up 9.5% QoQ, 167% YoY), and a record 5.43% EBITDA margin. Volume fell to 5,278 tons (down 9.5% QoQ, 6.5% YoY) because trade-route disruption and material shortages hit April and May. Management said June volume alone was 2,200 tons and supply had normalised, and it cut FY27 volume growth guidance to 12-15% from about 15-20%. Margin gains in April-May came from shortage-driven realisations across commodity and value-added products, and management guided to 5-5.5% EBITDA margin for the rest of the year.

financial_highlights.change: Lower volume; no YoY figure stated
Commodity exports are the bulk of this
Relates to FY2022-23 supplier registration cancellation; company plans to contest in tribunal

segments.name: Commodity (copper scrap-based)
segments.commentary: Management said margins improved across commodity and value-added products during the shortage. Commodity exports are the main part of the 18% export share.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: 63% of Q1 sales, the highest so far. Target is 63-64% for FY27, rising about 1-2% a year toward 68-69% over 3-4 years. About 250 tons of tin-coated product sold in Q1, with about 600 tons estimated for data centers.

segments.name: Copper business restructuring (Tieramet)
segments.commentary: All copper business moves from Bhagyanagar Copper to new wholly-owned subsidiary Tieramet Limited, then Bhagyanagar Copper merges into the parent and Tieramet is demerged. Parent keeps three city land parcels and the windmill project. NCLT hearing is set for 7 August 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth cut to 12-15% (from about 15-20%), attributed to roughly 2 months of lost sales in April-May; June run-rate of 2,200 tons is cited as support.
FY27 average realisation expected about 30% higher YoY and above the ₹1,300/kg plan average.
EBITDA margin guided at 5-5.5% for FY27; management said 5.5% for the full year may be difficult.
FY27 exports guided at 12-15% of sales (minimum 10%).
Long-term target of ₹5,000 crore revenue by FY30 reiterated, with volume growth of about 15% from FY28 onward.
Capex of about ₹40 crore over FY27-FY28; 10,000 ton capacity addition (35,000 to 45,000 tons) expected around April-June 2027, more likely June 2027.
Debt projected at ₹300-350 crore by FY30 (about ₹325 crore cited later).
capex_capacity: 35,000 metric tons of capacity has been added and is online now.
A further 10,000 tons (35,000 to 45,000 tons) is planned, expected operational around April-June 2027, more likely June 2027.
CTC wire capacity is about 80 tons per month, moving to 150 tons per month after a new 48-conductor machine (earlier about 28 conductors).
Two Hyderabad units: a 4-acre and a 60-acre facility. Capex of ₹40 crore is planned over FY27-FY28.
demand_pricing: Management cites third-party data: India copper consumption about 2.4 million tons by 2030; secondary copper demand to double from 0.7 to 1.4 million tons in five years.
Recycled copper market in India said to grow at 12-13% CAGR by some estimates; overall copper market 5-6% (or about 8.5% in other reports). Company says it is growing at 2-2.5x the market rate.
Primary copper refining charges have turned negative; Indian primary producers (Vedanta, Hindalco, Adani) are buying recycled copper.
Margins are set as a percentage of LME: raw material purchases at 86-95% of LME. Management says percentage margin is more stable than rupees per kg.
Data center: 800V DC architecture could cut copper bus bar demand by about 50%; management said this would have no material impact on the company.

Customers added: Crompton Greaves, TMC and Atlanta (transformers); Blue Star, Micron, OBO and L&T (Al data center bus bars). More than 100 tons of bus bars exported to North America in the last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Has sourcing normalised, and is 15-20% volume growth still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June normalised supply, so FY27 volume growth is now guided at 12-15%. Average realisation is expected to be about 30% higher YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 EBITDA per kg so high, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to shortage-driven realisations in April-May across commodity and value-added products, not exports. From June, margins are back to a normal 5-5.5% range.

qa_highlights.question: What was the GST impact of ₹17-18 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Surendra Bhutoria said it relates to FY2022-23 scrap purchases from a supplier whose registration was cancelled retrospectively. ₹17 crore was deposited and the company is contesting the case at the tribunal, which it believes it will win.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company's value-added mix changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added share is targeted at 63-64% for FY27, rising gradually toward 68-69% over 3-4 years. Management said it will not jump as it did in the last two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 5,000 crore FY30 revenue target and debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated ₹5,000 crore by FY30 regardless of copper price. Debt is projected at ₹300-350 crore by 2030, and management says the 5% EBITDA margin cash flow will fund growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fundraise timing and purpose?
qa_highlights.answer: First tranche of ₹52 crore is finalised, with funds expected in August. A second tranche is expected around March after the demerger. Management said MCX margin funding depends on copper prices.

risks_watch: Volume: June run-rate of 2,200 tons must be sustained to reach 12-15% FY27 growth.
Margin sustainability: 5.43% Q1 margin was helped by April-May shortage pricing; management guides 5-5.5% for the rest of the year.
Restructuring: NCLT hearing on 7 August 2026 and the Tieramet demerger, with the second fundraise tranche tied to demerger completion.
GST: ₹17 crore deposit on FY2022-23 input credit reversal, pending tribunal outcome.
Data center demand risk from shift to 800V DC architecture, which management says would have no material impact.
MCX margin requirements could rise sharply if copper prices rise, per management.
key_quotes: So, we should be looking at between 12% to 15% growth in terms of volume for the whole year now.

Going forward in the year, we hope to maintain the EBITDA margin between 5% and 5.5%. I think maintaining 5.5% for the whole year might be a little difficult, but we will be able to maintain between 5% and 5.5%, as was earlier indicated.
But we are very confident of 5,000 crores by FY30, whatever the copper price.
So, we are very, very confident that we will win.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand, value-added scaling and the FY30 ₹5,000 crore target, but cautious and defensive on volume: guidance was cut to 12-15% and management pointed to the June run-rate. Evasive on the GST matter (confident of tribunal win), the real estate inquiries (dismissed as belonging to a separate company), and on whether Q1 margins are repeatable, where it said 5.5% for the full year may be difficult.

adds.what: CTC wire capacity move to 150 tons/month via new 48-conductor machine (from ~80 t/month)

growth.why: FY27 volume growth was cut to 12-15% (from 15-20%) after April-May supply disruption, with FY27 realisation guided ~30% higher YoY, supporting moderate growth; the 10,000 t expansion is timed around June 2027 (about 4 quarters out), so it adds little to FY27.
